B1L12-G01-P271.title: Based on the pictures, complete the sentences with 用.

scene.alt: A person writing a letter in Chinese, marked ○, beside a letter starting “Dear mom”, marked ×.

repairs.note: 在 marks a place; the language you write in is a tool, so it takes 用: 用中文.

items.fallbackRepair: 用 + language + action: 用中文寫字. The picture marks Chinese ○ and English ×.

result.traditional: 他會用中文寫字，不會用英文寫字。
result.simplified: 他会用中文写字，不会用英文写字。
result.pinyin: Tā huì yòng Zhōngwén xiě zì, bú huì yòng Yīngwén xiě zì.
result.english: He can write in Chinese, but not in English.

scene.alt: Phone call beside a boy writing on paper.

repairs.note: 給 marks the person you call (給朋友打電話); the phone is the tool, so 用手機.
在 marks a place; a phone is a tool you use: 用手機.
He doesn’t like writing letters; with the phone he makes calls: 打電話.

items.fallbackRepair: 用 + tool + action: 用手機打電話.

result.traditional: 他喜歡用手機打電話，不喜歡寫信。
result.simplified: 他喜欢用手机打电话，不喜欢写信。
result.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yòng shǒujī dǎ diànhuà, bù xǐhuan xiě xìn.
result.english: He likes calling on his phone; he doesn’t like writing letters.

scene.alt: Two desks: a man on a phone with a laptop, and a person waving at a laptop.

repairs.note: 跟 marks a person you do something with; a phone or computer is a tool: 用.
在 marks a place; a phone or computer is a tool you use: 用.

items.fallbackRepair: 用 + tool before each action; the pictures show the phone for calls and the computer for work.

result.traditional: 他常用手機打電話，也常用電腦工作。
result.simplified: 他常用手机打电话，也常用电脑工作。
result.pinyin: Tā cháng yòng shǒujī dǎ diànhuà, yě cháng yòng diànnǎo gōngzuò.
result.english: He often makes calls on his phone and often works on his computer.

repairs.note: B answers with a thing (手機), so ask 什麼, not 誰.
跟 asks who you do it with; B names a tool, so ask with 用.
什麼 already makes it a question, so no 嗎.

items.fallbackRepair: The question word stays where the answer goes: 用 + 什麼 + action.

result.traditional: 你用什麼照相？
result.simplified: 你用什么照相？
result.pinyin: Nǐ yòng shénme zhàoxiàng?
result.english: What do you take photos with?

B1L12-G02-P272.title: Complete the sentences with 以前 or 以後 based on the pictures.

scene.alt: A schoolgirl and an arrow to a woman teacher at a blackboard.

repairs.note: The picture goes from student to teacher, and teacher is now, so the student came before: 以前.
She is a teacher now; before, the picture shows a student.

items.fallbackRepair: Time word before the verb: 以前是學生.

result.traditional: 我以前是學生，現在是老師。
result.simplified: 我以前是学生，现在是老师。
result.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián shì xuéshēng, xiànzài shì lǎoshī.
result.english: I used to be a student; now I’m a teacher.

scene.alt: Taiwan and an arrow to a US map with a laptop.

segments.traditional: 哥哥現在在台灣工作，他
segments.simplified: 哥哥现在在台湾工作，他

repairs.note: He works in Taiwan now and the arrow points to the US, so the US job is later: 以後.
已經 says it has already happened; the US job is still ahead: 以後要.
了 marks something done; a plan for later takes 要.

items.fallbackRepair: Time word first, then 要: 以後要去.

result.traditional: 哥哥現在在台灣工作，他以後要去美國工作。
result.simplified: 哥哥现在在台湾工作，他以后要去美国工作。
result.pinyin: Gēge xiànzài zài Táiwān gōngzuò, tā yǐhòu yào qù Měiguó gōngzuò.
result.english: My older brother works in Taiwan now; later he’s going to work in the US.

scene.alt: A teapot and cup, an arrow, then a cup of coffee.

repairs.note: The picture goes from tea to coffee, and coffee is now, so tea was before: 以前.
現在 is already the coffee; the tea in the first picture was before: 以前.
Coffee is what she likes now; the first picture shows tea.

items.fallbackRepair: 以前 before 喜歡, and the drink from the first picture: 以前喜歡喝茶.

result.traditional: 姐姐以前喜歡喝茶，她現在喜歡喝咖啡。
result.simplified: 姐姐以前喜欢喝茶，她现在喜欢喝咖啡。
result.pinyin: Jiějie yǐqián xǐhuan hē chá, tā xiànzài xǐhuan hē kāfēi.
result.english: My older sister used to like tea; now she likes coffee.

scene.alt: A person sick in bed, an arrow, then a woman jogging.

segments.traditional: 她最近常常生病，她決定
segments.simplified: 她最近常常生病，她决定

repairs.note: A decision is about what comes next: 以後.
She is often sick, so she should exercise more: 多, not 少.
Before a verb, “more” is 多: 多運動. 很 goes before adjectives.

items.fallbackRepair: 以後 + 要 + 多 + verb: 以後要多運動.

result.traditional: 她最近常常生病，她決定以後要多運動。
result.simplified: 她最近常常生病，她决定以后要多运动。
result.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn chángcháng shēngbìng, tā juédìng yǐhòu yào duō yùndòng.
result.english: She has been sick a lot lately; she has decided to exercise more from now on.

repairs.note: B gets off work at six, so dinner comes after: 以後.
以後 follows the clock time here: 六點以後, not 晚上.
B answers, so give the time, not the question word 幾點.

items.fallbackRepair: Clock time first, then 以後: 六點以後.

result.traditional: 我每天六點下班，六點以後吃晚飯。
result.simplified: 我每天六点下班，六点以后吃晚饭。
result.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān liù diǎn xiàbān, liù diǎn yǐhòu chī wǎnfàn.
result.english: I get off work at six every day and eat dinner after six.

segments.traditional: 你是什麼時候來台灣的？
segments.simplified: 你是什么时候来台湾的？

repairs.note: Before 年, two is 兩: 兩年.
B is already in Taiwan, so the coming was in the past: 以前.
A asks when B came, which is in the past: a period + 以前.

items.fallbackRepair: Period of time first, then 以前: 兩年以前 (two years ago).

result.traditional: 我是兩年以前來台灣的。
result.simplified: 我是两年以前来台湾的。
result.pinyin: Wǒ shì liǎng nián yǐqián lái Táiwān de.
result.english: I came to Taiwan two years ago.

segments.traditional: 十點了，中明還沒來，他遲到了。
segments.simplified: 十点了，中明还没来，他迟到了。

repairs.note: 十分 is a clock minute (十點十分); an amount of time is 十分鐘.
He hasn’t arrived yet, so his arrival is still ahead: 以後.
已經 is for what is done; he hasn’t arrived yet: 十分鐘以後.

items.fallbackRepair: Amount of time first, then 以後: 十分鐘以後.

result.traditional: 我給他打電話了，他說十分鐘以後會到。
result.simplified: 我给他打电话了，他说十分钟以后会到。
result.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā dǎ diànhuà le, tā shuō shí fēnzhōng yǐhòu huì dào.
result.english: I called him; he said he’d be here in ten minutes.

scene.alt: A classroom, an arrow, then two children riding bicycles.

repairs.note: In the first picture class is over and everyone is packing up: 下課.
The arrow goes from class to the bikes, so the ride comes after: 以後.
The first picture is the classroom, not a meal.

items.fallbackRepair: The event first, then 以後: 下課以後, not 以後下課.

result.traditional: 下課以後，我們去騎腳踏車。
result.simplified: 下课以后，我们去骑脚踏车。
result.pinyin: Xiàkè yǐhòu, wǒmen qù qí jiǎotàchē.
result.english: After class, we go bike riding.

scene.alt: Hands being washed, an arrow, then a girl eating.

repairs.note: The arrow goes from washing to eating, so washing comes before the meal: 以前.
The second picture shows a meal, not sleep.
The second picture shows a meal, not a class.

items.fallbackRepair: The event first, then 以前: 吃飯以前, not 以前吃飯.

result.traditional: 吃飯以前，我都會洗手。
result.simplified: 吃饭以前，我都会洗手。
result.pinyin: Chīfàn yǐqián, wǒ dōu huì xǐ shǒu.
result.english: I always wash my hands before I eat.

scene.alt: A girl brushing her teeth, an arrow, then a girl asleep.

repairs.note: The second picture shows her asleep in bed, not getting up: 睡覺.
The arrow goes from brushing to sleeping, so brushing comes before: 以前.
The second picture shows sleep, not work.

items.fallbackRepair: The event first, then 以前: 睡覺以前.

result.traditional: 我睡覺以前要刷牙。
result.simplified: 我睡觉以前要刷牙。
result.pinyin: Wǒ shuìjiào yǐqián yào shuāyá.
result.english: I have to brush my teeth before I go to sleep.

scene.alt: A graduate, an arrow, then a woman doctor.

repairs.note: The arrow goes from graduation to the doctor, so the job comes after: 以後.
The second picture shows a doctor (white coat, stethoscope): 醫生.

items.fallbackRepair: The event first, then 以後: 畢業以後想當醫生.

result.traditional: 我畢業以後想當醫生。
result.simplified: 我毕业以后想当医生。
result.pinyin: Wǒ bìyè yǐhòu xiǎng dāng yīshēng.
result.english: After I graduate, I want to be a doctor.

repairs.note: The restaurant is too far, so it is not convenient: 不方便.
給 marks who receives something; “for us” after a judgment is 對我們.

items.fallbackRepair: 對 + the people affected, then 都 and the comment: 對我們都不方便.

result.traditional: 那家餐廳太遠了，對我們都不方便。
result.simplified: 那家餐厅太远了，对我们都不方便。
result.pinyin: Nà jiā cāntīng tài yuǎn le, duì wǒmen dōu bù fāngbiàn.
result.english: That restaurant is too far; it’s inconvenient for all of us.

segments.traditional: 說了很多話，可是有的我不太懂。
segments.simplified: 说了很多话，可是有的我不太懂。

repairs.note: “Say to someone” is 對 + person + 說; 給 goes with 打電話 or 寫信.
在 marks a place; the person spoken to takes 對: 對我說.

items.fallbackRepair: He is the speaker and I’m the one who didn’t understand: 他昨天對我說.

result.traditional: 他昨天對我說了很多話，可是有的我不太懂。
result.simplified: 他昨天对我说了很多话，可是有的我不太懂。
result.pinyin: Tā zuótiān duì wǒ shuō le hěn duō huà, kěshì yǒude wǒ bú tài dǒng.
result.english: Yesterday he said a lot to me, but I didn’t really understand some of it.

alternatives.traditional: 昨天他對我說了很多話，可是有的我不太懂。
alternatives.simplified: 昨天他对我说了很多话，可是有的我不太懂。
alternatives.pinyin: Zuótiān tā duì wǒ shuō le hěn duō huà, kěshì yǒude wǒ bú tài dǒng.
alternatives.english: Yesterday he said a lot to me, but I didn’t really understand some of it.

repairs.note: “Good or bad for” is 對…好: 對身體很好, not 給.

items.fallbackRepair: 對身體 comes before the comment; exercise is good for you, too many sweets are not.

result.traditional: 運動對身體很好，吃太多甜點對身體不好。
result.simplified: 运动对身体很好，吃太多甜点对身体不好。
result.pinyin: Yùndòng duì shēntǐ hěn hǎo, chī tài duō tiándiǎn duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
result.english: Exercise is good for your health; eating too many sweets is bad for your health.

repairs.note: How you treat someone is 對 + person + 很好, not 給.

items.fallbackRepair: 要他 means she tells him to rest, so 李太太 is the one who 對李先生很好; then 下班以後.

result.traditional: 李太太對李先生很好，下班以後常常要他多休息。
result.simplified: 李太太对李先生很好，下班以后常常要他多休息。
result.pinyin: Lǐ tàitai duì Lǐ xiānsheng hěn hǎo, xiàbān yǐhòu chángcháng yào tā duō xiūxi.
result.english: Mrs. Li is very good to Mr. Li; after work she often tells him to rest more.

B1L12-G04-P282.title: Read the article and answer the questions. / Complete the dialogues with V 過了.

segments.traditional: 我去義大利、德國、法國的時候，會說他們的語言。
segments.simplified: 我去义大利、德国、法国的时候，会说他们的语言。

repairs.note: In France he speaks their language: 法文.
In France he speaks their language: 法文.
He speaks their language there, so he has spoken French: no 沒.

items.fallbackRepair: 過 goes right after the verb, before the object: 說過法文.

result.traditional: 去過，他在法國說過法文。
result.simplified: 去过，他在法国说过法文。
result.pinyin: Qùguo, tā zài Fǎguó shuōguo Fǎwén.
result.english: Yes, he has; he has spoken French in France.

segments.traditional: 我也學了一點兒日文跟印尼文。
segments.simplified: 我也学了一点儿日文跟印尼文。

repairs.note: He learned a little Indonesian, so the answer is yes: 學過.
The article says 一點兒, not 很多.

items.fallbackRepair: Verb, 過, then how much: 學過一點兒.

result.traditional: 學過一點兒。
result.simplified: 学过一点儿。
result.pinyin: Xuéguo yìdiǎnr.
result.english: He has studied a little.

segments.traditional: 當記者很不錯，希望以後能當一個有名的記者。
segments.simplified: 当记者很不错，希望以后能当一个有名的记者。

repairs.note: 過 is negated with 沒, never 不: 沒當過.
For an experience he hasn’t had, use 沒 + verb + 過, with no 了.
A job you do takes 當: 當過記者.

items.fallbackRepair: 還沒 + verb + 過: 還沒當過.

result.traditional: 還沒當過，他希望以後能當記者。
result.simplified: 还没当过，他希望以后能当记者。
result.pinyin: Hái méi dāngguo, tā xīwàng yǐhòu néng dāng jìzhě.
result.english: Not yet; he hopes he can be a reporter in the future.

segments.traditional: 我記得你今天有中文課，你
segments.simplified: 我记得你今天有中文课，你

segments.traditional: 還沒，我上的是晚上的課。
segments.simplified: 还没，我上的是晚上的课。

repairs.note: A asks whether today’s class is done: V過了嗎, with no 沒.
不 doesn’t go with 過; ask 上過了嗎.

items.fallbackRepair: Verb, 過, then 了: 上過了嗎.

result.traditional: 我記得你今天有中文課，你上過了嗎？
result.simplified: 我记得你今天有中文课，你上过了吗？
result.pinyin: Wǒ jìde nǐ jīntiān yǒu Zhōngwén kè, nǐ shàngguo le ma?
result.english: I remember you have Chinese class today. Have you had it yet?

segments.traditional: 你很不舒服吧？要不要去看醫生？
segments.simplified: 你很不舒服吧？要不要去看医生？

repairs.note: The doctor already gave B medicine, so B has seen one: no 沒.
看醫生 means seeing a doctor; the medicine is what the doctor gave.

items.fallbackRepair: Verb + 過 + object, then 了 at the end: 看過醫生了.

result.traditional: 我看過醫生了，醫生給了我三天的藥。
result.simplified: 我看过医生了，医生给了我三天的药。
result.pinyin: Wǒ kànguo yīshēng le, yīshēng gěi le wǒ sān tiān de yào.
result.english: I’ve already seen a doctor; the doctor gave me three days of medicine.

segments.traditional: 我今天晚上要跟朋友去吃飯，不能做晚飯了。
segments.simplified: 我今天晚上要跟朋友去吃饭，不能做晚饭了。

repairs.note: Zhongming means she already said it, so no 沒.
Mom hasn’t cooked; Zhongming means she already said so: 說過了.
不 doesn’t go with 過; say 說過了.

items.fallbackRepair: Verb, 過, then 了: 說過了.

result.traditional: 媽，妳說過了，妳忘記了嗎？
result.simplified: 妈，你说过了，你忘记了吗？
result.pinyin: Mā, nǐ shuōguo le, nǐ wàngjì le ma?
result.english: Mom, you already said that. Did you forget?

repairs.note: The link before 時候 is 的; 得 follows a verb to say how it is done.
以後 means after; A asks when, so answer with 的時候.
B answers, so no question word: the activity + 的時候.

items.fallbackRepair: Activity first, then 的時候: 聽音樂的時候.

result.traditional: 我聽音樂的時候最開心。
result.simplified: 我听音乐的时候最开心。
result.pinyin: Wǒ tīng yīnyuè de shíhou zuì kāixīn.
result.english: I’m happiest when I listen to music.

segments.traditional: 你發燒的時候，會怎麼做？
segments.simplified: 你发烧的时候，会怎么做？

repairs.note: A asks about B, so B answers with 我.
The link before 時候 is 的; 得 follows a verb to say how it is done.

items.fallbackRepair: Who, the situation, then 的 + 時候: 我生病的時候.

result.traditional: 我生病的時候，都會多喝水、多休息。
result.simplified: 我生病的时候，都会多喝水、多休息。
result.pinyin: Wǒ shēngbìng de shíhou, dōu huì duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxi.
result.english: When I’m sick, I always drink more water and rest more.

segments.traditional: 你不上課的時候，都在做什麼？
segments.simplified: 你不上课的时候，都在做什么？

repairs.note: A asks about time with no class, and you can’t go play ball when you’re busy: 有空.
The link before 時候 is 的; 得 follows a verb to say how it is done.
以後 means after; for “when”, use 的 + 時候.

items.fallbackRepair: The situation first, then 的 + 時候: 有空的時候.

result.traditional: 有空的時候，我都去打球。
result.simplified: 有空的时候，我都去打球。
result.pinyin: Yǒu kòng de shíhou, wǒ dōu qù dǎ qiú.
result.english: When I’m free, I go play ball.
